title: Protect US fisheries with fair markets | Science
content: The US Magnuson–Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act establishes federal fisheries management to support the food supply, the economy, human health, and recreation (1). Section 312 of the act authorizes disaster assistance in the event of a natural disaster, such as a tropical storm that destroys fishing vessels or seafood processing infrastructure, or a technological disaster, such as an oil spill that shuts down a fishery (1). On 19 November 2025, US Representative Nancy Mace (R-SC) introduced House Resolution (HR) 6150 (2), legislation that would amend Section 312 of the act to classify economic hardship, caused by lawful or unlawful actions by a foreign entity, as a disaster that justifies co-opting disaster assistance funds as subsidies. The bill, which is under referral with the House Committee on Natural Resources for potential consideration, seeks to address legitimate sources of unfair foreign competition, including illegal fishing, forced labor, and predatory pricing. However, the government could protect fisheries more effectively by passing better regulations, increasing import monitoring and traceability efforts, and vigilantly enforcing antidumping laws that penalize foreign firms selling seafood into the US market below production costs.
